observation_summary: The method ArrayUtils.add(T[] array, T element) throws a ClassCastException when both arguments are null because it returns an Object[] instead of the expected type (e.g., String[]).
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by the absence of a validation check for the null-null case. The method cannot determine the component type of the array when both inputs are null, leading to an incorrect return type. Adding a guard clause to check for this condition and throw an IllegalArgumentException (as suggested in the bug report) is a classic 'Checking' defect fix.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'if both parameters are null, the add() method returns an Object[] array, hence the Exception.'
The bug report suggests: 'I think the method ought to be changed to throw IllegalParameterException when both parameters are null.'
The stack trace shows a ClassCastException: '[Ljava.lang.Object; cannot be cast to class [Ljava.lang.String;'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic is flawed, the root cause is the missing validation of input parameters, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
This is a local procedural fix (adding a guard) rather than a design-level capability change.
